sources.source: Google SRE Book — Monitoring Distributed Systems

items.item: The four golden signals of monitoring are latency, traffic, errors, and saturation.
Dashboards should include some form of the four golden signals.
Saturation includes predictive signals of impending saturation.

at.out: not needed for a data pipeline's golden signals; service-saturation framing stays out of scope here

items.item: Counter: monotonically increasing, reset only on restart; wrong for values that can decrease.
Gauge: arbitrary up/down value (temperature, memory, concurrent requests).
Histogram: bucketed observation counts plus a sum; classic vs native histogram formats.

sources.source: Prometheus — When to use the Pushgateway

items.item: The Pushgateway exists for jobs that cannot be pulled (short-lived batch jobs).
Pitfalls when misused as a general collector: single point of failure/bottleneck, loses up-based health, never forgets stale series.

sources.source: Prometheus — Metric and label naming / Instrumentation

items.item: Every unique label-value combination is a new time series; high-cardinality labels multiply series count.
Concrete cardinality guidance (below 10 typical, over 100 is a red flag).
Logs can optionally carry trace and span IDs for correlation with traces.
records-lag-max is the consumer-side fetch-manager metric for maximum consumer lag, published by the consumer.

The four golden signals (latency, traffic, errors, saturation) are the service-level base; a data pipeline's golden signals specialize them with freshness, backlog and consumer lag, which have no request/response service analogue.
A counter is cumulative and monotonically increasing, reset only on restart; wrong for anything that can decrease.
A gauge is a single value that can arbitrarily go up and down (queue depth, last-success timestamp).
A histogram records observations into configurable buckets plus a running sum; a quantile read off it is an estimate.
Averaging per-instance quantiles across machines is mathematically wrong.
Kafka's consumer lag is published by the consumer, not the broker, as records-lag-max.
The Pushgateway exists for batch jobs a pull scraper can't reach, but misusing it as a general collector creates a single point of failure, loses up-based health, and never forgets stale series.
Every unique label-value combination is its own time series; high-cardinality labels multiply series count, with concrete guidance (under ~10, over ~100 is a design problem).
OpenTelemetry's Logs spec lets a log record carry TraceId/SpanId for correlation with a trace of the same execution context.
A correlation key of run_id, task_id, asset and partition lets every record of one run be selected across independent processes.
